title: SDK call plumbing, prefetching and SLA-aware tool playbook (PRD sketch)
content:
Summary:

This is a lightweight PRD-sketch that stitches together three related needs we keep hitting in hosted streaming: (1) SDK-level plumbing for reliable tool invocations over incremental/partial streams, (2) a client-driven speculative prefetch and hedging model for tool dependencies to reduce perceived latency for mobile/edge clients, and (3) SLA-aware runtime heuristics (server-side and SDK-side) to gracefully degrade tool fidelity and ensure latency SLOs.

Why this is different from existing drafts: most hosted-api docs focus on framing partial output contracts, typed frames, or generic graceful degradation. This doc specifically proposes a combined telemetry-driven feedback loop between runtime and SDKs so the client and server negotiate prefetching, throttling, and tool-fidelity fallbacks in-band with minimal handshake overhead. The emphasis here is pragmatic: small wire additions + SDK helpers that developers can opt into without changing existing tool contracts.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Reduce 95th percentile tool-call latency observed by SDK-integrated apps by 20% for mobile clients in pilot workloads.
- Avoid increased host-side cost >5% for the same traffic by limiting prefetch aggressiveness with server-side throttles and telemetry.
- Provide a minimal SDK surface (JS + Python) that handles: speculative-prefetch hints, per-call idempotency tokens, structured partial-result stitching, and SLA-aware fallback policies.
- Add telemetry signals to the platform so product can recommend adaptive prefetch thresholds per-customer.

Non-goals:
- Replacing the full typed-frame protocol work (this should interoperate with typed frames, not duplicate it).
- Solving every mobile-offline sync pattern—keep the initial scope to synchronous streaming sessions with intermittent connectivity concerns.

Background / motivating examples:
- Mobile note-taking app: the assistant suggests a calendar slot and hits an external calendar-creation tool. The tool call adds a second round trip which frequently pushes the UI past acceptable interaction latency. Client can speculatively fetch calendar availability and prepare to commit, but needs coordination with server so speculative fetches don't blow up costs or race with canonical tool state.
- Search-rewrite + external reranker: tool call ordering matters; we can prefetch candidate re-ranker features while generation is still ongoing. SDKs should be able to express low-cost prefetch hints that the server can deprioritize or collapse.

Proposed primitives (wire + SDK):
- PREFETCH_HINT frame (client -> server): short tokenized hint saying "I will likely call tool T with args shaped like X; acceptable staleness = 500ms; max_cost_units = 2". Purpose: let runtime schedule low-cost background prefetches or local cache warms.
- ACTION_INVOCATION frame (stream / final): existing tool invocation frame plus two additions: idempotency_token and sla_priority (low|normal|high).
- CHECKPOINT / SNAPSHOT frame (server -> client): explicit partial result that can be committed locally; houses partial-structured output and an action-binding map. This allows SDK to render intermediate UI and reconcile with later final action results.
- TELEMETRY_EVENT frame: compact event samples for the session (e.g., tool_latency_ms, prefetch_hit, prefetch_cancelled, hedged_invocation_count). These are low-bandwidth and aggregated; SDK emits and server echoes aggregated signals back when requested.

Notes on wire format: keep frames as compact newline-delimited JSONL entries for streaming endpoints. Each frame must be < 1KB for hints and telemetry; larger payloads remain in existing action frames. Example (literal text we expect in stream):

{ "type": "PREFETCH_HINT", "tool": "calendar.lookup", "shape": "{date_range, user_id}", "staleness_ms": 500, "max_cost_units": 2 }
{ "type": "ACTION_INVOCATION", "tool": "calendar.create", "args_ref": "cid-42", "idempotency_token": "tok-abc-123", "sla_priority": "high" }
{ "type": "TELEMETRY_EVENT", "name": "prefetch_hit", "value": "1" }

The server should allow clients to send PREFETCH_HINT without counting against quota / billable tool invocations; actual tool execution only billed on ACTION_INVOCATION when it occurs.

Server-side heuristics (runtime):
- Prefetch admission controller: accepts or rejects hint based on customer config, recent prefetch CPI cost, and global server load. Response paths: ACCEPT / DEFER / REJECT. If DEFER, runtime can enqueue low-priority background prefetch with a best-effort expiry.
- Hedged invocation policy: when a tool is critical to meeting SLA and host latency spikes, runtime may invoke a cheaper fallback variant (lower-fidelity model or cached response) concurrently with primary tool and accept first completed. Preferences come from tool-variant graph and product configuration.
- Telemetry-based backpressure: aggregate per-customer prefetch success rate; if prefetches have low hit rate and high cost, reduce admission for that customer automatically.

SDK ergonomics (JS + Python): recommended minimal API
- client.prefetch(tool, hint, options) -> Promise<PrefetchHandle>
- PrefetchHandle.queryStatus() -> {state: prefetched|cancelled|deferred}
- client.invoke(tool, args, options) where options may include idempotency_token and sla_priority; returns streaming iterator/object that yields CHECKPOINT frames and final result.

Syntactic examples (JS sketch):
- const pre = await client.prefetch('calendar.lookup', {dateRange, userId}, {stalenessMs: 500, maxCostUnits: 2})
- for await (const chunk of client.invoke('calendar.create', {payload}, {idempotencyToken: pre.token, slaPriority: 'high'})) { renderChunk(chunk) }

SDK patterns to encourage (ergonomics notes):
- Opt-in prefetch: default off. Developers must opt into prefetching per route or via client config to avoid accidental cost increases.
- Light-weight handles: prefetch returns a tiny token that SDKs can pass into invoke; SDK avoids reserializing large shapes.
- Safe idempotency: SDK generates idempotency tokens per user action (not per session) so retries are safe across reconnections.
- Speculative UI composition: SDK exposes interim CHECKPOINT frames keyed by action id; client can render them optimistically and reconcile once final action result arrives.
- Cancellation: SDKs should expose a cancel(prefetchHandle) that notifies server to drop related background work.

Telemetry and observability: what we must capture
- Client emits: prefetch_requested, prefetch_accepted, prefetch_cancelled, prefetch_hit, action_invoke_start, action_invoke_end (latency_ms), action_invoke_fallback_used, session_reconnects.
- Server aggregates by customer+route and exposes: prefetch_accept_rate, prefetch_hit_rate, median_tool_latency_by_priority, hedged_invocation_rate, cost-per-prefetch-unit.
- Product-visible dashboard: per-customer prefetch panel, suggested prefetch thresholds, and a heatmap of prefetch cost vs hit-rate.

Success metrics (proposed):
- 95th percentile perceived tool-latency for opted-in SDK flows drops 20% within 8 weeks of pilot for 3 pilot customers.
- Prefetch hit rate >= 40% for pilot workloads (target adjustable).
- No >5% increase in billable tool invocation cost for pilot customers after server throttling and opt-in defaults.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): implement minimal PREFETCH_HINT and TELEMETRY_EVENT frame support on runtime (server-side accepts hints but ignores by default). SDK prototypes in JS only.
- Phase 1 (4–6 weeks): server admission controller + basic prefetch execution using existing cache/backing stores. SDK: JS + Python, opt-in client.prefetch API. Pilot with internal apps.
- Phase 2 (6–8 weeks): add hedged invocation policies, telemetry dashboards, and auto-throttle rules. Expand pilot to 3 external customers.
- Phase 3 (ongoing): extend to typed frames, mobile SDKs (Android/iOS), and hardened offline reconciliation patterns for private deployments.

Risks and mitigations:
- Cost blowups from naive prefetching: mitigation = opt-in only, server admission controller, per-customer caps, aggregated telemetry-based automatic throttles.
- Consistency / double-commit risk when speculative prefetch leads to a live tool commit: require idempotency tokens and server-side sequence checks; prefer prefetch for read-like operations only by default.
- Complexity in SDKs causing developer confusion: provide 1-page quickstart and a developer-playbook for decisions (when to prefetch vs not).

Open questions (needs engineering input):
- Should PREFETCH_HINT ever be billable as a low-weight unit (i.e., cheap metered unit) instead of free? Con: churn in billing infra and confusion. Pro: easier to limit abuse.
- How to encode "shape" for tool args in a compact way that is language-agnostic and cheap to compute on client? (protobuf-lite? canonical short schema id?)
- What backoff defaults should the SDK use for prefetch on intermittent connectivity?

Immediate next actions (owner: Maya):
- [ ] Sync with serving-runtime (Jonah) to validate admission controller feasibility (by 2025-02-18).
- [ ] Prototype minimal PREFETCH_HINT/TELEMETRY_EVENT parsing in streaming runtime (PR: platform/pull/789 reference).
- [ ] Draft SDK quickstart + example app for internal pilot (Sofia to lead).
- [ ] Create short UX checklist for product to adopt opt-in prefetch safely (Derek).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is an exploratory sketch; feedback sought on the tradeoffs: wire-minimal vs rich-typed frames, free-hint vs metered-hint, and SDK ergonomics that keep opt-in friction low.

Appendix: short checklist for integration testing:
- confirm PREFETCH_HINT is ignored by servers without the admission controller enabled (backwards compat).
- assert idempotency token semantics across reconnects and retry windows.
- verify telemetry events are emitted with packet sampling to avoid excessive client uplink.
- run cost simulation: generate prefetch hints at 10k qps and simulate acceptance rates (needed: infra test harness).

End of sketch.
